response.sql:
WITH side_counts AS (
  SELECT o.dealedge, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM riskandmargin AS r
  JOIN orders AS o
    ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.dealedge
), above_average AS (
  SELECT order_count
  FROM side_counts
  WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM side_counts)
)
SELECT SUM(order_count) AS total_counts,
       AVG(order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM side_counts)) AS average_excess
FROM above_average;

assumptions.assumption: Each matching risk/margin record counts its joined order, so an order with multiple matching records is counted multiple times. Orders without a matching risk/margin record are ignored.

alternatives.interpretation: Count each distinct order once per side, even if it has multiple matching risk/margin records.
alternatives.sql:
WITH side_counts AS (
  SELECT o.dealedge, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count
  FROM riskandmargin AS r
  JOIN orders AS o
    ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.dealedge
), above_average AS (
  SELECT order_count
  FROM side_counts
  WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM side_counts)
)
SELECT SUM(order_count) AS total_counts,
       AVG(order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM side_counts)) AS average_excess
FROM above_average;
